foodie.title: Brisket at Lewis Barbecue
foodie.description: Central Texas method transplanted to the Lowcountry — post oak, custom-built pits, and a brisket that justifies the queue.
foodie.bonus: Order the beef rib if they still have one when you reach the counter.

foodie.title: Oyster Counter at 167 Raw
foodie.description: A tiny walk-in-only counter working through Nantucket oysters, lobster rolls and a tuna burger that people queue an hour for.
foodie.bonus: Put your name down and go have a drink somewhere else while you wait.

foodie.title: Lunch Line at Bertha's Kitchen
foodie.description: A North Charleston cafeteria line run by the same family for decades — lima beans, fried chicken, okra soup and red rice, served on a tray.
foodie.bonus: Take whatever the woman working the line tells you to take.

foodie.title: Crab Rice at Hannibal's Kitchen
foodie.description: A family soul-food kitchen off Upper King serving Gullah staples since 1985 — crab rice, shark steak and okra soup, from breakfast onward.
foodie.bonus: Order the crab rice even if it is nine in the morning.

foodie.title: Oyster Roast at Bowens Island
foodie.description: A cinderblock shack on stilts over the marsh where they shovel steamed local clusters straight onto your table and hand you a knife.
foodie.bonus: Eat outside on the deck and stay for the sunset over the creek.

foodie.title: Dinner at Chez Nous
foodie.description: A hidden house on a side street with about thirty seats and a handwritten menu of two starters, two mains and two desserts that changes every single day.
foodie.bonus: Don't ask what's on the menu beforehand. That's the point.

foodie.title: Dinner at FIG
foodie.description: Food Is Good — a two-decade Charleston benchmark for Lowcountry ingredients cooked simply, and one of the hardest tables in the city to get.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the ricotta gnocchi even if it isn't listed that night.

foodie.title: Southern Larder Dinner at Husk
foodie.description: The restaurant that reset modern Southern cooking, in a Queen Street mansion where the menu is built only from ingredients grown below the Mason-Dixon line.
foodie.bonus: Have a drink in the bar building next door before you sit down.

foodie.title: Chef's Counter Dinner at The Ordinary
foodie.description: Feast on towers of oysters and seafood inside a converted 1920s bank turned raw bar and oyster hall.
foodie.bonus: Order something off the menu you can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Biscuits at Callie's Hot Little Biscuit
foodie.description: Grab a still-warm buttermilk biscuit from the walk-up window of this Charleston institution.
foodie.bonus: Order one flavor you've never tried before.

foodie.title: Noodles at Xiao Bao Biscuit
foodie.description: Slurp Asian street food classics inside a converted gas station on upper King Street.
foodie.bonus: Split a dish family-style with the table.

culture.title: RiverDogs Game at Riley Park
culture.description: Minor league baseball beside the Ashley River, with between-innings promotions that are the actual reason most people go.
culture.bonus: Stay for whatever ridiculous promotion runs between innings.

culture.title: Spoleto Festival USA
culture.description: For seventeen days the entire city becomes a venue — opera, chamber music, theatre and dance in churches, courtyards and the Dock Street Theatre.
culture.bonus: Buy a ticket for something in a genre you would never normally choose.

culture.title: International African American Museum
culture.description: Built on Gadsden's Wharf, where a very large share of enslaved Africans first landed in North America, the building raised on pillars so the ground stays untouched.
culture.bonus: Spend time in the African Ancestors Memorial Garden beneath the building.

culture.title: Charleston Wine + Food
culture.description: Five days in March when the Lowcountry food world takes over Marion Square and a hundred side venues, and every chef in the city is cooking outdoors.
culture.bonus: Skip the Culinary Village once and do a single small signature dinner instead.

culture.title: The Charleston Museum
culture.description: Founded in 1773 and generally reckoned the first museum in America, covering Lowcountry natural history, silver, and the city's own record of itself.
culture.bonus: Find the polar bear, then work out why it's there.

culture.title: Old Slave Mart Museum
culture.description: The last surviving slave auction building in South Carolina, now a museum telling the history of the domestic trade on the site where it happened.
culture.bonus: Read the building's own history panel before the exhibits.

culture.title: Aiken-Rhett House Museum
culture.description: A townhouse preserved rather than restored — peeling wallpaper left as found, and the enslaved people's quarters, kitchen and stable yard still standing behind it.
culture.bonus: Walk the back buildings before the main house, not after.

culture.title: Gibbes Museum of Art
culture.description: Charleston's art museum, strongest on American work connected to the South, plus a remarkable collection of miniature portraits.
culture.bonus: Find the miniature portrait gallery — it's easy to walk straight past.

chill.title: An Afternoon in Hampton Park
chill.description: The biggest park on the peninsula, laid out on the old racecourse grounds, with a rose garden, a duck pond and almost no tourists.
chill.bonus: Walk the full perimeter loop once before you settle anywhere.

chill.title: Morning Bun at Brown's Court Bakery
chill.description: A neighbourhood bakery on a residential corner of Harleston Village doing proper laminated pastry and a flat white worth sitting outside with.
chill.bonus: Take it to the churchyard bench a block away.

chill.title: Browse Blue Bicycle Books
chill.description: A King Street used bookstore with a deep Southern literature section and a rare-book room upstairs that most people never go into.
chill.bonus: Go upstairs and ask to see something from the rare room.

chill.title: Gardens at Middleton Place
chill.description: The oldest landscaped gardens in the United States, laid out in 1741 as terraces and butterfly lakes stepping down to the Ashley River.
chill.bonus: Walk out to the butterfly lakes and look back up the terraces.

chill.title: Golden Hour on the Pitt Street Bridge
chill.description: The remains of the old trolley bridge to Sullivan's Island, now a pier into the marsh where locals walk dogs and watch the light go.
chill.bonus: Stay until the marsh grass turns orange.

chill.title: Sunset Sail on Charleston Harbor
chill.description: Go out under sail from the Maritime Center and watch the peninsula, the Ravenel Bridge and Fort Sumter go past from the water.
chill.bonus: Ask to help raise the mainsail.

chill.title: Stroll Waterfront Park's Pineapple Fountain
chill.description: Wander the live oak-lined promenade along the harbor and cool off at the iconic Pineapple Fountain.
chill.bonus: Sit on a porch swing facing the water for ten quiet minutes.

chill.title: Sunset at the Battery / White Point Garden
chill.description: Watch the sun drop over the harbor from the Battery's historic seawall promenade.
chill.bonus: Guess which mansion along the row you'd pick to live in.

chill.title: Cortado at Second State Coffee
chill.description: Settle in with a cortado at this minimalist local roaster on upper King Street.
chill.bonus: Strike up a conversation with the barista about their roast of the week.

chill.title: Garden Wander at Magnolia Plantation
chill.description: Walk 500-year-old romantic gardens draped in Spanish moss along the Ashley River.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest labeled camellia in the garden.

8ball.title: Pick a Street and Follow It to the Water
8ball.description: Choose any street south of Calhoun you have never walked down, and follow it until it dead-ends at water. Whatever is there is the plan.
8ball.bonus: Take every alley and cut-through you pass on the way.

8ball.title: Cross the Harbor and Eat Wherever You Land
8ball.description: Take the water taxi from the Maritime Center across to Patriots Point, then walk inland from the dock and eat at the first place that looks busy.
8ball.bonus: No reviews, no searching. First busy room wins.

social.title: Live Music at the Royal American
social.description: A low-slung roadhouse on the Morrison Drive industrial strip with a covered porch, cheap drinks and a genuinely good booking calendar.
social.bonus: Get there early enough to sit on the porch before the set.

social.title: Rooftop Beers at Revelry Brewing
social.description: A small East Side brewery whose rooftop deck looks straight back at the peninsula skyline, with a taplist that turns over constantly.
social.bonus: Get up to the roof before sunset, not after.

social.title: Bowling and Shuffleboard at the Alley
social.description: A downtown bowling alley with shuffleboard, arcade cabinets and a kitchen doing bar food well above the standard the room suggests.
social.bonus: Play shuffleboard rather than bowling if the lanes are full.

social.title: PBR and Tots at the Recovery Room
social.description: A gloriously unpretentious dive that reliably sells more cans of Pabst than almost any bar in America, with tater tots to match.
social.bonus: Order the tot-chos for the table.

social.title: Work Your Way Up King Street
social.description: One of the densest bar strips in the Southeast — start below Calhoun and move north, one drink per room, until the crowd changes character.
social.bonus: Only go into places you have never been.

social.title: Cocktails at the Gin Joint
social.description: A dark East Bay room doing pre-Prohibition drinks properly, with a Bartender's Choice card where you name four adjectives and they build from that.
social.bonus: Order off the Bartender's Choice card and don't specify a spirit.

social.title: Late Night at the Belmont
social.description: An Upper King bar with pressed tin, a film projector running silent movies on the brick, and one of the best classic cocktail programmes in town.
social.bonus: Sit where you can see the projection wall.

social.title: Rooftop at Stars
social.description: An Upper King rooftop with steeple views across the peninsula and a bar that stays busy long after the dining room downstairs empties.
social.bonus: Find the corner of the deck that looks straight down King Street.

social.title: Browse the Charleston City Market
social.description: Wander the historic open-air market and watch sweetgrass basket weavers at work.
social.bonus: Talk to one vendor about how they learned their craft.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at The Vendue
social.description: Watch the harbor lights come on from the rooftop bar of this art-filled boutique hotel.
social.bonus: Order the drink with the silliest name on the menu.

social.title: Trivia Night at Edmund's Oast
social.description: Grab a flight of house-brewed beer and battle it out at trivia night at this upper King Street brewery.
social.bonus: Team up with the table next to you if you're short a player.

social.title: Ghost Tour Through the French Quarter
social.description: Walk cobblestone streets after dark on a guided ghost tour through Charleston's most haunted blocks.
social.bonus: Ask your guide for the one story they refuse to tell on rainy nights.

adventure.title: Ferry to Bulls Island and Boneyard Beach
adventure.description: A ferry from Garris Landing into Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, then a three-mile walk across the island to a beach of salt-bleached skeleton trees.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length of Boneyard Beach before the return ferry.

adventure.title: Hike the Awendaw Passage
adventure.description: The coastal terminus of the Palmetto Trail, running seven miles of tidal creek edge and pine flatwoods out of Buck Hall on the Intracoastal.
adventure.bonus: Turn around at the first creek overlook and walk it in both directions.

adventure.title: Beach Day on Sullivan's Island
adventure.description: Wide, uncrowded sand with no high-rises and no commercial strip — park on a residential street, walk over the dunes, and that is the day.
adventure.bonus: Walk down to the Station 28 end where the crowd thins out.

adventure.title: Kiteboarding Lesson at Isle of Palms
adventure.description: Steady onshore wind and warm shallow water make this coast one of the friendliest places in the country to learn to fly a kite and get up on a board.
adventure.bonus: Stay out until you can ride twenty yards in one direction.

adventure.title: Boneyard Beach at Botany Bay
adventure.description: An Edisto Island wildlife preserve where a drowned maritime forest stands in the surf, reachable on a free permit and a half-mile walk.
adventure.bonus: Go at sunrise when the light comes through the dead trunks.

adventure.title: Paddle to the Morris Island Lighthouse
adventure.description: Kayak out through the Folly River marsh to a brick lighthouse standing alone in open water, cut off from its island by a century of erosion.
adventure.bonus: Time it for low tide so you can stand on the sandbar beside it.

adventure.title: Boardwalk the Blackwater at Beidler Forest
adventure.description: A mile and a half of boardwalk through the largest remaining stand of virgin bald cypress and tupelo anywhere, some of it a thousand years old.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every bench and just listen for five minutes.

adventure.title: Watch Dolphins Strand Feed at Kiawah
adventure.description: Kiawah's bottlenose dolphins drive fish onto the mud bank and beach themselves to eat — a hunting behaviour practised almost nowhere else on earth.
adventure.bonus: Get there on a falling tide and wait rather than walking the bank.

adventure.title: Sunset Run Along the Battery Seawall
adventure.description: Run the flat waterfront path along the Battery with harbor views the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Pick a stranger's pace and try to match it for one block.

adventure.title: Sunrise Surf Session at Folly Beach
adventure.description: Rent a board and catch a sunrise surf lesson at Folly's laid-back, locally loved break.
adventure.bonus: Stay in the water for one more wave than you planned.

adventure.title: Boat Tour to Fort Sumter
adventure.description: Ride the ferry across Charleston Harbor to where the first shots of the Civil War were fired.
adventure.bonus: Read one placard out loud to whoever you're with.

adventure.title: Walk the Angel Oak Boardwalk
adventure.description: Walk the boardwalk beneath a 400-plus-year-old live oak with limbs that touch the ground.
adventure.bonus: Find the biggest limb and take a photo lying beside it.

adventure.title: Kayak Shem Creek at Sunset
adventure.description: Paddle a kayak past dolphins and shrimp boats on Shem Creek as the sky turns pink over Mount Pleasant.
adventure.bonus: Wave at every shrimp boat captain you pass.

adventure.title: Bike the Ravenel Bridge
adventure.description: Pedal the dedicated bike and pedestrian lane across the soaring Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge.
adventure.bonus: Stop at the highest point for a photo over the harbor.

adventure.title: Paddleboard James Island County Park
adventure.description: Rent a paddleboard and glide across the calm marsh-lined lake at James Island County Park.
adventure.bonus: Paddle to the far shore and back without touching down.
